title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, fix a time and place, say you're on your way (or running late), and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to Part 2. From here on the course is about the Odia you'll use with friends and around town, starting with the conversation you'll have most often: **making plans**. Free tonight? Let's go out. Where shall we meet? I'm on my way. Sorry, stuck in traffic. Another day?

Close friends of the same age in Odisha soon switch to **ତୁ**, so this unit teaches the ତୁ forms properly (ତୁ ଅଛୁ, ତୋ, ତୋତେ, the bare command ଆ! 'come!' and the 'do it later' form ଫୋନ କରିବୁ 'give me a call'). You'll also practise 'let's' and 'shall we?' with **ଚାଲ** and the -ବା form, and the phrases for 'I'm on my way', 'just leaving' and 'I was about to…'. And of course the English words every young Odia uses for this: **ଫ୍ରି, ପ୍ଲାନ୍, ଲେଟ୍, ୱିକେଣ୍ଡ୍**.

vocab.note: ଫ୍ରି ଅଛୁ? 'are you free?' The native way is ସମୟ ଅଛି? 'do you have time?'
ପ୍ଲାନ୍ କରିବା 'to make a plan'. Much more everyday than ଯୋଜନା. With an ending it loses the hasanta: ପ୍ଲାନରେ (planôre).
ୱିକେଣ୍ଡରେ "at the weekend". Or simply ଶନି-ରବି "Sat–Sun".
Also ତୋର (torô). The ତୁ set: ତୁ "you", ତୋ / ତୋର "your", ତୋତେ "(to) you".
ତୋତେ ଫୋନ କରିବି 'I'll call you'. Compare ତୁମକୁ (familiar), ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ (formal).
ଚାଲ, ଯିବା "come on, let's go". Polite: ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ. Among friends often clipped to ଚାଲ୍ (chal).

vocab.en: to go out (for a wander), go out somewhere
vocab.note: The classic Odia 'going out': ସଞ୍ଜରେ ବୁଲିବାକୁ ଯିବା? 'shall we go out this evening?'

vocab.en: to hang out and chat (with friends)
vocab.note: ଆଡ୍ଡା 'a long relaxed chat, hanging out'. Also ଆଡ୍ଡା ଦେବା.
ସିନେମା ଦେଖିବା 'to watch a film'; ସିନେମା ହଲ୍ 'cinema hall'. Young people also say ମୁଭି.
ପାର୍ଟି ଦେବା 'to throw a party / treat everyone' — expected when you get a job, pass an exam or have a birthday.
Object form ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ "(to) everyone".
The everyday reaction to a good idea: ବଢ଼ିଆ! 'great!'

vocab.en: to get together, join (in); to mix
vocab.note: ସମସ୍ତେ ମିଶି 'all together'; ତୁ ବି ମିଶିବୁ? 'will you join us?'
ପକ୍କା? 'for sure?' — ପକ୍କା! 'definitely!'
ଅଧ is the form of ଅଧା "half" used before a noun.
ବାଇକରେ 'by bike'. Any two-wheeler, including a scooty.
ମୋତେ ମନେ ପକାଇଦେବୁ 'remind me (will you)'. Compare ମନେପଡ଼ିବା 'to remember (come to mind)'.
Same meaning as ଶୀଘ୍ର, which sounds more careful.
ବାହାନା କରିବା 'to make excuses'.
ବାଟ "way" + -ରେ. ବାଟରେ ଅଛି "I'm on my way".
With the continuous it means 'just about to / right now': ଏଇ ବାହାରୁଛି 'just leaving'. ଏଇମାତ୍ର 'just a moment ago'.
ପ୍ରାୟ ପହଞ୍ଚିଗଲି 'I'm almost there'; ପ୍ରାୟ ସାତଟା 'about seven'.
ଟ୍ରାଫିକ୍ ଜାମ୍ "traffic jam".
ଟ୍ରାଫିକରେ ଫସିଛି 'I'm stuck in traffic'; ଫସିଗଲି 'I got stuck'.
ଲେଟ୍ ହେବା 'to be late', ଲେଟ୍ କରିବା 'to make (someone) late, be late'. Same as ଡେରି.
ମୋର ମୁଡ୍ ନାହିଁ 'I'm not in the mood'; ମୁଡ୍ ଖରାପ 'in a bad mood'.
ଆରାମ କରିବା 'to relax, rest'.

phrases.note: Familiar: ଫ୍ରି ଅଛ? · Formal: ଆପଣ ଫ୍ରି ଅଛନ୍ତି?

phrases.en: Let's meet at the junction at seven.
For sure, right? / Is it confirmed?
I'll be there in five minutes.
phrases.note: Odia uses the present continuous for something about to happen, just like English "I'm arriving in five".

phrases.en: Sorry, I'll be a bit late.
phrases.note: ସରି (English "sorry") is what friends say; ମାଫ କରିବେ is for strangers and elders.
To a ତୁ-friend: ଅପେକ୍ଷା କର୍ (kôr), or simply ରହ୍, ଆସୁଛି! "hang on, coming!"

phrases.en: Can't make it today, let's do another day.
I'm not in the mood today.

grammar.title: Let's … and shall we …?: ଚାଲ + the -ବା form
grammar.body:
In Unit 17 you met the ଆମେ-future in **-ବା**: ଆମେ ଯିବା 'we'll go'. With friends this one form does three jobs:

**Let's** — put **ଚାଲ** 'come on' in front: ଚାଲ, ସିନେମା **ଯିବା** 'let's go to a film'. ଚାଲ alone also works: ଚାଲ! 'let's go!' With elders use ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ.
**Shall we?** — say the -ବା form as a question, with or without କି: ଚା **ପିଇବା**? 'shall we have tea?', ଆଜି ବାହାରେ **ଖାଇବା କି**? 'shall we eat out tonight?'
**What / where / when shall we…?** — question word + -ବା: କ'ଣ **କରିବା**? 'what shall we do?', କେଉଁଠି **ଭେଟିବା**? 'where shall we meet?', କେତେବେଳେ **ବାହାରିବା**? 'when shall we leave?'

**Let's not** — add ନାହିଁ: ଆଜି ଯିବା ନାହିଁ 'let's not go today'.
**We'll see** — ଦେଖିବା (lit. 'we'll see'), the classic non-committal answer.

In casual speech some people use **-ବୁ** for 'we' (ଚାଲ ଯିବୁ); both are understood. **Trap**: -ବା here is not the dictionary form of the verb even though it looks the same; context (ଚାଲ, a question mark, ଆମେ) makes it clear.

examples.en: Come on, let's go to a film today.
Shall we go to Puri on Saturday?
What shall we do this evening?
It's raining, let's not go today.
Let's have some tea. (to someone older)

grammar.title: Talking to a close friend: ତୁ forms and "do it later"
grammar.body:
With close friends of your age (and younger siblings), Odias use **ତୁ**. Don't use it with anyone older or anyone you've just met; there ତୁମେ or ଆପଣ is right. The pronoun set:
ତୁ — you · ତୋ / ତୋର — your · ତୋତେ — (to) you · ତୋ ପାଇଁ — for you

**Verbs with ତୁ** end in **-ଉ** (the same endings as ଆମେ):
ତୁ ଅଛୁ? 'are you?' · ତୁ କ'ଣ କରୁଛୁ? 'what are you doing?' · ତୁ କେବେ ଆସିଲୁ? 'when did you come?' · ତୁ ଆସିବୁ? 'will you come?' · ତୁ ଖାଇଛୁ? 'have you eaten?'

**Commands with ତୁ** are the bare stem: **ଆ** 'come', **ଯା** 'go', **ଖା** 'eat', **ଦେ** 'give', **ନେ** 'take', **କର୍** 'do', **ବସ୍** 'sit', **ଶୁଣ୍** 'listen'. Compare ତୁମେ: ଆସ, ଯାଅ, ଖାଅ, ଦିଅ, ନିଅ, କର, ବସ, ଶୁଣ.

**'Do it later' commands** use the future: ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ **କରିବୁ** 'call me when you get there' (ତୁ), **କରିବ** (ତୁମେ), **କରିବେ** (ଆପଣ). This sounds softer than a bare command, and it is how you give instructions for later.

**Don't**: future + ନାହିଁ is the usual friendly way: ଲେଟ୍ **କରିବୁ ନାହିଁ** 'don't be late'. In fast speech ନାହିଁ often shrinks to **-ନି** joined to the verb: ମୁଁ ଜାଣେନି 'I dunno', ସେ ଆସିନି 'he hasn't come', ହେବନି 'won't happen'. The careful forms with ନାହିଁ are always correct.

examples.en: What are you doing? Come quickly!
Give me a call when you get there.

grammar.title: On the way, just leaving, about to…
grammar.body:
**On the way**: ମୁଁ **ବାଟରେ** ଅଛି 'I'm on my way'.

**Present continuous for 'right now / any minute'**: ଆସୁଛି 'coming!', ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟରେ ପହଞ୍ଚୁଛି 'there in five'. Add **ଏଇ** for 'just': **ଏଇ** ବାହାରୁଛି 'just leaving', ଏଇ ଆସୁଛି 'coming right now'.

**About to**: verbal noun in **-ବାକୁ** + **ଯାଉଛି** (the same pattern as 'it's going to rain' in Unit 13): ସିନେମା ଆରମ୍ଭ ହେବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି 'the film's about to start'.

**Was about to / was just going to**: **-ବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲି**: ମୁଁ ତୋତେ ଫୋନ କରିବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲି! 'I was just about to call you!' Or simply the past continuous: ମୁଁ ବାହାରୁଥିଲି 'I was (just) leaving'.

**Already**: the ending **-ଣି** added to a past form means 'already / by now': ମୁଁ ବାହାରିଗଲି**ଣି** 'I've already left', ପ୍ରାୟ ପହଞ୍ଚିଗଲି**ଣି** 'I'm nearly there'. (More on -ଣି in Unit 22.)

**Trap**: 'I'm on my way' is never ମୁଁ ବାଟ ଅଛି; you need -ରେ.

examples.en: I'm on my way, ten minutes.
I was just about to call you!

dialogue.title: Saturday night
dialogue.setting: Thursday at the office canteen in Bhubaneswar, Rohit and Sam plan the weekend. Then Saturday, 6:40 pm, Sam is outside Esplanade mall on the phone.

lines.speaker: Rohit
lines.en: Sam, are you free Saturday night?

lines.speaker: Rohit

lines.speaker: Sam

lines.speaker: Sam

lines.speaker: Rohit
lines.native: ମୁଁ ବାହାରୁଥିଲି, ହେଲେ ବୋଉ ଦୋକାନରୁ କ୍ଷୀର ଆଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ…
lines.roman: muṃ baharuthili, hele bou dokanôru khyirô aṇibaku kôhile…
lines.en: I was just leaving, but Mum asked me to get milk from the shop…

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ବାହାନା! ଜଲଦି ଆ। ମୁଁ ଭିତରକୁ ଯାଉଛି।
lines.roman: bahana! jôldi a. muṃ bhitôrôku jauchhi.
lines.en: Excuses! Hurry up. I'm going in.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଉ, ହେଲେ ଆଜି ପପକର୍ନ ପଇସା ତୁ ଦେବୁ!
lines.roman: hôu, hele aji pôpkôrn pôisa tu debu!
lines.en: Fine, but the popcorn's on you tonight!

culture:
Plans in Odisha are flexible. 'Seven o'clock' often means half past, and ଏଇ ଆସୁଛି 'coming right now' can mean anything up to half an hour, so most people confirm with a call or a WhatsApp just before leaving (ପକ୍କା ତ?). It's normal to bring along a friend or cousin without asking, and whoever suggested the outing, or has just had good news, is expected to pay or give a **ପାର୍ଟି**; otherwise friends usually split the bill.

In Bhubaneswar the classic meeting points are a well-known *chhak* (junction: Master Canteen, Jayadev Vihar, Vani Vihar), a mall such as Esplanade One, or a favourite tea stall; in Cuttack it's the riverside or the old Chandni Chowk lanes. Going out for its own sake, a drive on a scooty, an ice cream, tea by the Mahanadi, is ବୁଲିବାକୁ ଯିବା, and the long evening chats are ଆଡ୍ଡା. When cancelling, give a reason and suggest another day (ଆଜି ହେବ ନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଦିନେ); a flat 'no' sounds cold. With older people, and when you've only just met someone, keep to ତୁମେ or ଆପଣ: switching to ତୁ is something friends drift into, often after the other person does it first.

tip.title: Talking to a close friend: ତୁ
tip.body:
- With close friends your age: **ତୁ** 'you', **ତୋ / ତୋର** 'your', **ତୋତେ** '(to) you'.
- ତୁ-verbs end in **-ଉ**: ତୁ ଅଛ**ୁ**? · କ'ଣ କରୁଛ**ୁ**? · ଆସିବ**ୁ**? · ଗଲ**ୁ**?
- Never use ତୁ with someone older or someone you've just met.

sentences.en: Are you free tomorrow?
What are your plans for the weekend?
What are you up to right now?
I'll call you later.

sentences.native: ନା, ଏ ୱିକେଣ୍ଡରେ ମୁଁ ଫ୍ରି ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: na, e wikeṇḍôre muṃ phri nahiṃ.

Will you come on Sunday?

sentences.en: We don't have a plan, you tell us.
Where did you go yesterday?

tip.title: Let's… / Shall we…?
tip.body:
- **Let's**: **ଚାଲ** + the ଆମେ-future in **-ବା**: ଚାଲ, ସିନେମା **ଯିବା**.
- **Shall we?** Just ask with -ବା: ଚା **ପିଇବା**? · ବାହାରେ **ଖାଇବା କି**?
- **What / where shall we…?**: କ'ଣ **କରିବା**? କେଉଁଠି **ଭେଟିବା**?
- To an elder: **ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ**.

sentences.en: Let's watch a film tonight.
Shall we go out this evening?
What shall we do on Sunday?
Great plan! Is everyone coming?

sentences.native: ଚାଲ, ଛକରେ ଚା ପିଇ ଆଡ୍ଡା ମାରିବା।
sentences.roman: chalô, chhôkôre cha pii aḍḍa mariba.
sentences.en: Let's have tea at the junction and hang out.

sentences.native: ଶନିବାର ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗର ଜନ୍ମଦିନ ପାର୍ଟି ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: sônibarô mo saṅgôrô jônmôdinô parṭi ôchhi.
sentences.en: There's a friend's birthday party on Saturday.
Shall we eat out today?
Call everyone and tell them.

sentences.native: ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଛି, ଆଜି ବୁଲିବାକୁ ଯିବା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: bôrsa heuchhi, aji bulibaku jiba nahiṃ.

sentences.en: Fix a time first.

Will you join us too?

tip.title: Commands to a friend, now and later
tip.body:
- ତୁ-commands are the bare stem: **ଆ** 'come', **ଯା** 'go', **ଦେ** 'give', **କର୍** 'do', **ଶୁଣ୍** 'listen'.
- For **later**, use the future: ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ **କରିବୁ** (ତୁ) / **କରିବ** (ତୁମେ).
- **Don't**: future + ନାହିଁ: ଲେଟ୍ **କରିବୁ ନାହିଁ**.
tip.pattern: ଆ! · ଯା! · ଫୋନ କରିବୁ · … କରିବୁ ନାହିଁ

sentences.en: Hurry up, everyone is waiting!
Call me when you get there.

sentences.native: ମୋ ପାଇଁ ଟିକେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କର, ମୁଁ ଗାଧୋଉଛି।
sentences.roman: mo paiṃ ṭike ôpekhya kôrô, muṃ gadhouchhi.
sentences.en: Wait for me a bit, I'm in the shower.
No more excuses, come on!
Give me a call when you leave home. (familiar)
Give me my bike keys.
Listen, don't be late today.

sentences.native: ତୁ ଆଗରେ ଯା, ମୁଁ ପଛରେ ଆସୁଛି।
sentences.roman: tu agôre ja, muṃ pôchhôre asuchhi.
sentences.en: You go ahead, I'm right behind you.
Don't forget the tickets!

tip.title: On the way, just leaving, about to
tip.body:
- **ମୁଁ ବାଟରେ ଅଛି** 'I'm on my way'.
- **ଏଇ** + continuous = 'just / right now': ଏଇ ବାହାରୁଛି.
- **About to**: -ବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି. **Was about to**: -ବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲି.
- **Already**: -ଲି**ଣି**: ବାହାରିଗଲିଣି 'I've already left'.

sentences.native: ଚିନ୍ତା କର ନାହିଁ, ମୁଁ ବାଟରେ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: chinta kôrô nahiṃ, muṃ baṭôre ôchhi.
sentences.en: Don't worry, I'm on my way.

sentences.native: ଏଇ ଘରୁ ବାହାରୁଛି, ଦଶ ମିନିଟରେ ପହଞ୍ଚୁଛି।
sentences.roman: ei ghôru baharuchhi, dôsô miniṭôre pôhôñchuchhi.
sentences.en: Just leaving home, I'll be there in ten minutes.
The bus is about to leave, hurry!
I was just about to come over to yours!
I'm nearly there, I'm near the junction.
The traffic on the roads is terrible today.

sentences.native: ଅଧ ଘଣ୍ଟା ହେଲା ମୁଁ ଏଠି ଫସିଛି।
sentences.roman: ôdhô ghôṇṭa hela muṃ eṭhi phôsichhi.
sentences.en: I've been stuck here for half an hour.

sentences.native: ତୁ କେଉଁଠି ଅଛୁ? ସିନେମା ଆରମ୍ଭ ହେବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି।
sentences.roman: tu keuṃṭhi ôchhu? sinema arômbhô hebaku jauchhi.
sentences.en: Where are you? The film's about to start.
I've just left.

tip.title: Cancelling nicely
tip.body:
- Say sorry (**ସରି** with friends), give a reason, and offer another day: ଆଜି ହେବ ନାହିଁ, **ଆଉ ଦିନେ**.
- Soften with **ଟିକେ**: ଟିକେ ଲେଟ୍ ହେବ.
- A bare ନା sounds cold; ମୁଡ୍ ନାହିଁ is fine only with close friends.

sentences.en: Sorry, I got held up a bit at the office.

sentences.native: ତୁମେମାନେ ଆରମ୍ଭ କର, ମୁଁ ଲେଟ୍ ଆସିବି।
sentences.roman: tumemane arômbhô kôrô, muṃ leṭ asibi.
sentences.en: You lot start, I'll come late.

sentences.native: ସରି, ଆଜି ହେବ ନାହିଁ। କାଲି ଯିବା?
sentences.roman: sôri, aji hebô nahiṃ. kali jiba?
sentences.en: Sorry, can't today. Shall we go tomorrow?

sentences.native: ମୋ ଦେହ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ, ଆଜି ଘରେ ଆରାମ କରିବି।
sentences.roman: mo dehô bhôlô nahiṃ, aji ghôre aramô kôribi.
sentences.en: I'm not feeling well, I'll rest at home today.

sentences.native: ମୋର ଆଜି ବାହାରକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ମୁଡ୍ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: morô aji baharôku jibaku muḍ nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I'm not in the mood to go out today.
The plan's off because of the rain.
No problem, we'll go another day.

sentences.native: ଆଜି ପୂରା ଦିନ ଆରାମ, କିଛି ପ୍ଲାନ୍ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: aji pura dinô aramô, kichhi plan nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Lazy day today, no plans.
